passage: Come, sit, Tanuja. Sabina Aunty will tell you about the terrace. I was fifteen, and the whole class was recording a dance on the school terrace parapet. Everyone was cheering. I climbed up because saying no felt scarier than the drop. My knees shook and my smile was painted on. Down below, Roopa stayed on the floor and said, "No thanks, it's not for me. I'll hold your bag." And nobody stopped talking to Roopa. Nobody even blinked. I looked at her calm face and then at the edge, and I climbed down. That evening Roopa and I shared a packet of chips on the stairs like always, and the video went ahead without me.

qa.q: Where did the students record the dance?
qa.a: They recorded the dance on the school terrace parapet.

qa.q: What was Sabina feeling on the parapet with shaking knees?
qa.a: Frightened but wanting to belong; the cheering pulled Sabina up while the shaking knees showed fear.

qa.q: What choice did Sabina make after seeing Roopa's refusal?
qa.a: Sabina climbed down from the parapet, seeing that Roopa's calm no cost no friendships.

qa.q: How might Roopa have felt saying no thanks in front of the class?
qa.a: Probably nervous but steady; offering to hold the bag shows a kind, friendly way to refuse.

grounding: A teenager joins a risky viral dance to fit in until a friend says no thanks and stays friends.

passage: Ten minutes before the school bus, the group crowded around the fountain in the courtyard. The challenge was to balance on the wet stone rim while a friend filmed. Everyone else had done it already. "Your turn, Kalyani, come on!" Kalyani's stomach flipped, but stepping up felt easier than being the only one who didn't. The rim was slick with morning rain and one foot slid. Francis caught Kalyani's sleeve. "You're fine. Honestly, I'm skipping mine, I'll film instead. No offence!" "None taken," someone laughed, and the filming went on. Kalyani stepped down, heart racing, and noticed nobody thought less of Francis. The bus horn sounded and they ran to it together.

qa.q: What was the rim of the fountain slick with?
qa.a: The rim was slick with morning rain.

qa.q: Why did Kalyani step up onto the rim even though the stomach flipped?
qa.a: Kalyani wanted to belong and feared being the only one who didn't; that outweighed the fear of slipping.

qa.q: What small step could Kalyani take next time?
qa.a: Say no thanks lightly like Francis and offer another role, such as filming.

qa.q: How do the others see Francis's choice to film instead?
qa.a: They accept it easily, laughing none taken, and Francis stays part of the group without doing the challenge.

grounding: A teenager joins a risky challenge to fit in, and a friend who says no thanks and stays friends shows other options.

passage:
Monday. The corridor dance was everywhere: the whole of 10B filming it on the wet back stairs after rain, sliding down the last three steps in socks. Devika watched Damini and the others practise and felt her face go warm when someone said, "You're not doing it?"
Wednesday. She did it. Socks, wet steps, phone held up by Mehek. On the third step her foot shot out and she landed on her hip, hard. Everyone cheered because it looked dramatic. Damini had said, "No thanks, I'll hold your bag," and then held it. Damini also walked her to the class teacher, who sent her to the school nurse and banned filming on those stairs that same afternoon.
Saturday. Devika's video had 600 views and a purple bruise. At the chai stall Damini handed her a samosa. "You know I'd have been your friend anyway," Damini said. Devika felt oddly relieved.

qa.q: What did Damini offer to do instead of the dance?
qa.a: She said, "No thanks, I'll hold your bag," and then held it.

qa.q: Why did Devika join the dance on the wet stairs?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and left out when asked if she wasn't doing it, and wanted to belong with the class more than she worried about slipping.

qa.q: What went right after Devika fell?
qa.a: Damini took her to the class teacher the same day, so the nurse checked her hip and filming on the risky stairs was stopped.

qa.q: How did Damini see the dance and their friendship?
qa.a: Damini did not want to risk the stairs but stayed close, holding the bag, getting help and sharing a samosa, showing that saying no did not mean leaving Devika.

grounding: It illustrates a teenager who joins a risky trend to fit in, and a friend who says no thanks and stays a friend.

passage: Simran, you think these challenges are new? In 1989, when your Amandeep Bua was fifteen, the craze in Ludhiana was riding a bicycle with no hands down the canal bridge. Every boy did it, and then the girls started. I had never wanted to, not even a little, but Jaspreet and the others did it every evening and I stood watching like a lamp post. So one Sunday I did it. Halfway down my front wheel wobbled and I scraped my palms along the railing. I still have the mark, see? My friend Parminder had said, "No thanks, I'll wait at the bottom," and she waited, with her dupatta to wrap my hand. She walked me straight home, and my mother cleaned the cuts and asked why. I said, "Everyone was doing it." She said, "Parminder wasn't." That stayed with me.

qa.q: Where did the craze take place?
qa.a: On the canal bridge in Ludhiana.

qa.q: Why did Amandeep ride with no hands even though she did not want to?
qa.a: She felt left out standing and watching while her friends did it, and wanted to belong more than she feared falling.

qa.q: What was the key choice in the story that turned out wise?
qa.a: Parminder's choice to say no thanks yet wait at the bottom showed there was another way to stay part of the group without taking the risk.

qa.q: How might Parminder have felt waiting at the bottom of the bridge?
qa.a: She was probably nervous watching her friend and caring enough to be ready with her dupatta, and not at all less of a friend for saying no.

grounding: It illustrates a teenager joining a risky craze to fit in, and a friend who said no thanks and still stayed a friend.

passage: The school bus was leaving in ten minutes and it had started to drizzle. Rekha's group had decided this was the day for the new lip-sync trend: stand on the low wall by the railway footbridge, arms out, while a train passes behind. Everyone had one except Rekha and Kavitha. "Come on, Rekha, quick, before the train!" Rekha's heart thudded. She climbed onto the wet wall. It was slippery. She looked down at Kavitha. Kavitha shook her head. "No thanks. I'll film you from here, but I'm staying on the ground." Somehow that made it easier. Rekha climbed down. "Me too, from here," she said. The others groaned, then shrugged. The train roared past and they all danced on the pavement, laughing, rain in their hair. They got the bus with a minute to spare, and Kavitha sat next to her.

qa.q: Where did the group want to film the lip-sync trend?
qa.a: On the low wall by the railway footbridge.

qa.q: What was Rekha feeling as she stood on the wet wall?
qa.a: Rekha felt nervous and pressured, her heart thudding, torn between wanting to fit in and knowing the wall was slippery.

qa.q: What helped Rekha change her mind?
qa.a: Kavitha's calm "No thanks" and offer to film from the ground showed there was a safe way to still take part.

qa.q: How might the others in the group have seen Rekha climbing down?
qa.a: They groaned at first, perhaps disappointed, but then shrugged and joined the pavement dance, which suggests they did not really mind.

grounding: It illustrates a teenager tempted to join a risky trend to fit in, and a friend whose no thanks shows fitting in has safer options.

passage: In their Ghaziabad housing society, everyone in Class 9 was doing the same dance trend that week, and the version getting the most views was filmed on a terrace parapet with the city behind. Jyoti had the song stuck in her head all day. At four she messaged Chandrika: "Terrace at 5? Parapet version?" Chandrika replied, "No thanks. I'll film you on the ground though." Jyoti felt a sting. Was Chandrika calling her silly? On the terrace the wind pulled at her dupatta, and the drop looked much deeper than on screen. Chandrika stood by the stairs, phone ready, not arguing, just waiting. Jyoti stepped back. "Courtyard?" "Courtyard," Chandrika grinned. They did it eleven times, until they kept laughing mid-spin. The courtyard version got fewer views. Jyoti watched it twice before bed anyway.

qa.q: Where was the most-viewed version of the dance filmed?
qa.a: It was filmed on a terrace parapet with the city behind.

qa.q: What did Jyoti feel when Chandrika said "No thanks"?
qa.a: Jyoti felt a sting of hurt, wondering if Chandrika thought the idea was silly.

qa.q: What did Chandrika's response show about fitting in?
qa.a: By refusing only the risky part, offering to film on the ground and staying friendly, Chandrika showed Jyoti could join the trend without the danger.

qa.q: How might Chandrika have felt standing by the stairs?
qa.a: Chandrika was probably worried about the drop but chose to wait calmly rather than argue, trusting Jyoti to decide.

grounding: It illustrates a teenager drawn to a risky version of a viral dance to fit in, and a friend who says no thanks, stays friends and shows another way to belong.
